**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "The UK's number one tea subscription." | **Unsupported.** This is a superlative and a market-rank claim. It isn't on the allowlist and no source was supplied. It also invites an ad-platform or ASA challenge, since "number one" needs evidence of the ranking. |
| "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time." | Allowlisted. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25." | Allowlisted. |
| "Tea Subscription UK" (headline) | Plain descriptor, no claim. |

**Other notes**
- The landing page must also make the pause/cancel and free-delivery claims, since an ad can't claim more than its page does.
- You gave no character limit. If this is a Google RSA, descriptions cap at 90 characters, and this one is about 116, so it would be rejected. Check against the real limit.
- No slop-list words, exclamation marks or fake urgency.

**Suggested replacement for the description**
> Loose leaf tea and plastic-free tea bags, monthly. Pause or cancel any time. Free UK delivery over £25.

Every claim in it is allowlisted. If you want a ranking claim, send the source (a named survey or report, with date) and I'll add it. Otherwise use `[PROOF NEEDED: source for "number one" ranking]`. If the 90-character limit applies, drop the first sentence or shorten the delivery line.
